correctness.rationale: For every fixed prime \(p\equiv1\pmod6\), an order-three unit \(r\) exists. For finite sets \(Q\) of primes \(q\equiv r\pmod p\), exact CRT counts make the events \(p\parallel m\) and \(q\parallel m\) independent Bernoulli events with probabilities \(\delta_q=(q-1)/q^2\). The count \(Z_Q\) has mean \(\mu_Q\to\infty\) by reciprocal-prime divergence and variance at most \(\mu_Q\). Chebyshev yields \(\Pr(Z_Q\le1)\le\mu_Q/(\mu_Q-1)^2\), tending to zero. Two distinct witnesses force \(p^2\mid\sigma(m^2)\), contradicting the equality when \(p\parallel m\). Thus \(\mathscr A\cap\{p\parallel m\}\) has density zero. For every finite set \(P\) of primes \(p\equiv1\pmod6\), the set \(\mathscr A\), up to a zero-density subset, avoids all \(p\parallel m\) and has upper density at most \(\prod_{p\in P}(1-\delta_p)\). This product tends to zero as \(P\) grows, since \(\sum_{p\equiv1\pmod6}\delta_p=\infty\). Both finite-modulus and infinite limits are performed in the correct order; finite regression tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Primary source arXiv:2202.08116v1 labels density zero an open conjecture. Meyerowitz (MathOverflow 369441) gave a conditional product heuristic with the same local obstruction, but not a proof of the infinite intersection. The new finite-CRT plus Chebyshev lemma resolves this gap without exchanging nonuniform limits, establishing the full density-zero theorem. The closest public squarefree-family result gives only a lower bound and explicitly leaves the density question untouched. Publication priority remains subject to unindexed literature.
